The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-3,-1],$ the line segment for $x\in [-1,0),$ and the line segment for $x\in [0,3].$ Therefore, we write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,0).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 1) \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-0.5.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+2)(3) \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =2-0.5+4.5 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
